verdicts.candidate: N5_vgh|VG_R|lb252|sk21|M|h0.06|tax1 (value/growth 12-1 switch, 6% hysteresis, monthly, tax-managed 1% budget)
reasons: It is a frozen growth tilt. The holdings replay from 2000-07 shows switches only at losses (2000-03 and 2008-12), then 100% IWF from 2009 to 2026: 13 trades in 26 years and no tax paid during the run. Starts in value years stay frozen in value: 2013 start -3.04 pp/yr to the end, 2016 -1.21, 2020-23 starts -0.3 to -1.8.

Static IWF on the same windows scores higher (+1.21 vs +1.16 in CA). Rule minus IWF: 5y -0.19 (rule ahead in 28% of windows), 10y -0.25 (34%), to-end -0.80 (23%). All of the rule's edge over static growth comes from 2000-05 starts escaping the 2000-02 crash; every start year from 2006 on trails static IWF. With later first starts (2004-2014), static IWF scores +1.80 to +2.66, against +1.01 to +1.16 for the rule.

Long protocol (VIVAX/VIGRX vs VFINX, 119 starts 1994-2023) fails in CA: score +0.61, full +0.79, 10y beat 60%, boot_p 0.224. 10-year windows starting 1994-96 beat VFINX 0 of 12, because the rule was frozen in 1990s growth through 2000-02. Static VIGRX does better (+0.67/+0.92). On the long protocol 0 of 15 neighbours pass, and 5 have negative full excess (-0.96 to -1.18).

Other style pairs, exact rule, CA: only 3 of 11 clear bar 1-3, all S&P 500/900 large-cap (SPYV/SPYG +1.04, IUSV/IUSG +0.45, IVE/IVW +0.53). 6 of 11 are negative: IJS/IJT -0.37, IWS/IWP -0.54, RPV/RPG -0.83, VBR/VBK -1.65, IWN/IWO -1.72, RZV/RZG -3.41. In every large-cap pair the static growth leg scores higher than the rule.

Placebo: 40 random date-determined IWD/IWF switching paths through the same tax-managed execution. 4 of 40 clear bar 1-3 in CA; the candidate's score ranks about 93rd percentile and its full excess about 72nd. The tax freeze alone produces passes.

Neighbourhood on full CA: 20 of 38 pass, but the failures are structured. All no-hysteresis versions fail (-0.31 to +0.31). Lookbacks 189 and 315 at sk21/h0.06 fail the 10y and 15y beat rates. Lookback 126 scores -0.15. Quarterly, every-2-months and standard execution all fail.
boot_p depends on the first-start path: 0.026 from 2000-07, 0.113 with the first start in 2012, 0.998 from 2014. Deflated Sharpe given ~12,000 trials is 0.012 in CA.

Pre-tax signal information is weak: next-month chosen-minus-other +2.97%/yr, t=1.45 (2000-26), and negative over 2009-16. Own-history signals in small and pure-style pairs show none (IJS/IJT t=-1.36). The CA rule cannot harvest it anyway, because it is frozen.

Mechanical tests hold: offsets (CA score +0.86 to +1.16), 1-day lag (+1.22), 35 bps costs (+1.10), distribution-tax realism (+1.93 to +1.96), and start dates shifted by 1 and 2 months (+1.24 / +1.15). They hold because it barely trades, so they do not rescue it.
bugs_found: metrics.summary computes boot_p and max_dd from the first start's path only. For tax-frozen strategies that is the luckiest path (it escaped 2000-02 at a loss). Moving the first start moves boot_p from 0.026 to 0.113 (2012) and 0.998 (2014).

verify.battery silently drops the 2000-2010 sub-period when the first start is after 2000-01-01, because it looks for an exact window start of 2000-01-01. N5_vgh's first start is 2000-07, so the one sub-period where its timing paid is hidden.

No look-ahead and no execution bug found: proxy signals are lagged by 1 day; the 1-day execution lag improves it; wash-sale guard OK. StyleRotation's hysteresis state (_held) tracks the target rather than the actual frozen holdings. That is by design, not a bug, but it means the signal and the book diverge.

verdicts.candidate: Tax-managed cyclical season, Oct 1-May 1 boundary (G19 cyclicals Oct1-May1 / SPY TAX gb=0.01)
reasons: It is a ratchet into a static, XLK-heavy cyclical tilt. Holdings by start: 2000-01 ends about 80% cyclicals (XLK 31%); 2003-07 ends 97% SPY; 2009-07 100% SPY; 2013-01 82% cyclicals; 2013-07 54% SPY. To-end excess for 2009-2023 starts averages about +0.03 pp/yr (range -0.68 to +0.74). Sub-periods in CA: 2000-10 +2.43, 2010-20 +0.32, 2020-26 -1.29.

The never-rebalanced four SPDRs score higher (+1.21 vs +0.85 in CA). Rule minus static: 10y -0.33 (rule ahead in 30%), to-end -0.70 (16%), and for starts from 2003 on the rule is ahead in only 7% of to-end windows. The same basket held all year with the same tax-managed execution and no season gets +0.99 / full +0.97 / 10y 100% / boot_p 0.077. With first starts in 2002-2014 the static basket beats the rule every time, and the rule's boot_p rises to 0.459 (2004) and 0.979 (2014).

Long protocol (Fidelity Select twin, Oct 1-May 1, 1986-2026; not run in round 1) fails in CA: +1.89, full +0.75, 10y beat 78%, boot_p 0.146. Static buy-and-hold of the same four funds does better (+2.44, boot_p 0.048), and the seasonal rule beats it in only 16% of 10-year windows. With the alternative Fidelity maps, the season beats static only for alt2 in CA. Fidelity Selects are survivors, so even the static excess is inflated.

Same rule on other sector sets, CA: iShares IYC/IYJ/IYM/IYW (same sectors, different index) fails on 10y beat (73%); Vanguard VCR/VIS/VAW/VGT fails (boot_p 0.243); no-tech +0.40 fails; IGV for XLK fails (boot_p 0.20); cyclicals ex-tech with XLF/XLE -0.08. Only the XLK and SMH baskets pass.

Placebos: 14 of 16 random season windows with the same basket and execution are positive in CA (median +0.42), and 5 of 16 clear bar 1-3. Non-Halloween windows such as 6/15-2/15 and 7/15-3/15 are positive too. The season is mostly irrelevant after tax; the reversed season scores -0.17.

Neighbourhood: all 12 boundary pairs are positive (+0.45 to +0.85), and the candidate is the post-hoc best of them. Gain budget 0 does better (+1.00, boot_p 0.013): never realizing a gain is buy-and-hold plus loss-switching, not seasonality.
The pre-tax seasonal effect has vanished: in-season vs out-of-season basket-minus-SPY was t=2.32 over 2000-26, but +0.80 vs +0.86 %/yr (t=-0.02) over 2017-26. Deflated Sharpe 0.015 in CA.

Mechanical tests hold: offsets (+0.83 to +0.91), 1-day lag (+0.82), 35 bps costs (+0.44), realism (+0.02), cover_tax (identical), and start dates shifted by 1 and 2 months (+0.84, boot_p 0.017 / +0.90, 0.012). So the quarterly start grid is not the source of the result.
bugs_found: First-start-path dependence of boot_p (metrics.summary): 0.030 from 2000-01, but 0.459 from 2004, 0.177 from 2010 and 0.979 from 2014.

The quarterly-start grid interacts with season boundaries: with Oct 1-May 1, 3 of 4 quarterly starts buy cyclicals first. I added the full_m1/full_m2 shifted protocols (registered in verify_tilts.py with setdefault) to test this. For this candidate it made no material difference.
The engine's 0%-interest January tax loan is not material here: cover_tax=True gives identical results (+0.85).

best_variant_numbers.note: Best-scoring neighbour (gain budget 0), NOT a fix: it is the same frozen static tilt, even more so (92 trades). It was run only on full CA and inherits every failure above.

summary:
Both candidates fail. In a taxable CA account each is a static tilt that the tax-managed execution freezes: growth for N5_vgh, an XLK-heavy cyclical basket for the Oct 1-May 1 season rule. Each beats its own static tilt only through one episode, the 2000-02 bear market, when holdings were at a loss and could be switched without tax. The mechanical checks all hold: rebalance offsets, 1-day lag, costs up to 35 bps, distribution-tax realism, cover_tax, and start dates shifted by 1 and 2 months. That is because the rules barely trade. The hindsight and regime tests break both.

N5_vgh (CA +1.16, full +1.83, boot_p 0.026, DSR 0.012):
- Static IWF scores higher (+1.21). The rule trails IWF in 66% of 10-year and 77% of to-end windows; every start from 2006 on trails static growth.
- Its 1994-2026 VIVAX/VIGRX twin fails (10y beat 60%, boot_p 0.224; 10-year windows starting 1994-96 win 0 of 12) and also loses to static VIGRX.
- On other style pairs it works only in S&P 500/900 large-cap V/G (3 of 11), where static growth scores higher; small, mid and pure-style pairs are negative.
- 4 of 40 random switching paths through the same execution also clear bar 1-3.

Cyclical season (CA +0.85, full +1.44, boot_p 0.030, DSR 0.015):
- The never-rebalanced basket scores higher (+1.21) and beats it in 84% of to-end windows (93% for starts from 2003 on).
- Its Fidelity twin with the Oct 1-May 1 boundary (1986-2026, not run in round 1) fails (boot_p 0.146) and loses to the static Fidelity basket.
- It fails with the same sectors from iShares or Vanguard, and without XLK.
- 14 of 16 random season windows are also positive after tax.
- The pre-tax seasonal effect is zero over 2017-26.

New code: research/lab/families/verify_tilts.py (random-path placebo signal; full_m1/full_m2 shifted-start protocols). Scripts and logs: research/lab/scratch/verify_tilts/. Write-up: research/lab/results/verify_tilts.md. 239 configs, 355 runs, plus two batteries.
open_questions: Should metrics.summary or the bar report boot_p across several first starts (e.g. the median over 2000-2014 first starts) instead of the single first path? For tax-frozen strategies the 2000 start is systematically the luckiest path, and that inflates confidence.

Static growth (IWF from 2004+) and static cyclicals (from 2002+) clear bar 1-3 when scored after the 2000-02 crash. That is the same launch-window and post-bubble hindsight that round 1 flagged for VUG and similar funds. Any recommendation of a static tilt needs the same pre-2000 and regime scrutiny.

The Fidelity Select long-history proxies are survivors with historical loads and redemption fees. Should long-history sector results be discounted, or checked against a non-survivor sector index (e.g. Ken French industry portfolios) before they count as pre-2000 evidence?

In NONE the pre-tax style momentum (VIVAX/VIGRX 1994-2026: +1.37, boot_p 0.059) and sector seasonality (Fidelity maps beat their static baskets) look weakly real. Is that worth pursuing for the user's tax-deferred accounts, or is it out of scope?
The trimmed grids (88-config vgh neighbourhood, 33/30-config cyc neighbourhood/placebo) were not run. They are unlikely to change the verdicts, given the static-dominance and long-history results.
